title: Knowledge check: Building Features End to End

questions.prompt: In Building Features End to End, which statement best describes Route definition?
options: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
Define required, optional and rejected values explicitly, validate types and constraints, and return a consistent client error before the data reaches business logic.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
questions.explanation: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Building Features End to End?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.
questions.answer_key: Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.
questions.explanation: Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.

questions.prompt: A change related to Building Features End to End appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
